question: Construct the next positive conservative finite reaction step with self-consistent temperature and H/He coefficient feedback; bind covariant energy/current identities through actual Wolfram+xAct execution.

assumptions.statement: A collision substep uses a fixed finite event matrix S, current physical packet energies, nonnegative initial comoving populations and thermal/radiation energy, and exact invariant rows L with LS=0.

The ground-state H/He family neglects heavy-nucleus recoil energy; active packets may be realized in equal ±p pairs. Recombination uses fixed positive captured-energy quadrature nodes with temperature-dependent nonnegative weights. Current collision data include fixed nonnegative angular weights and opposite momentum pairs representing the input state exactly, or packet-indexed event columns. The same angular rule defines the continuous collision field.
Thermal nuclei and thermal electrons share a nonrelativistic monatomic ideal temperature; c_v=3 k_B/2, Nthermal=Nnuc+Ne, Nnuc>0. Active electrons retain their own kinetic-energy inventory.

Proposal donors are evaluated at the initial state; temperature, composition and declared density coefficients are evaluated at the trial collision endpoint. At the initial point proposals equal the declared physical propensity.

Rates are finite continuous nonnegative on the constructed compact convex domain. T-singular rates use U0>0 and h cUbar<=U0; uniqueness/Picard requires the computed scaled-norm q<1. Initial zero donors disable only incident events.

Physical-ODE error bounds additionally require local Lipschitz vector field, quasipositivity on accessible domain boundaries, bounded time variation, and retention of the physical path in the same domain (sufficient h cUphysbar<=U0/2).

Any Coulomb-log coefficient is restricted to its declared positive interval 0<n_lo<=n<=n_hi<C^2. The selected count functional, volume, derivative bounds and interval self-map must be supplied together.

Geometry is prescribed diagonal Bianchi I with positive scale factors, metric (-+++), proper time in seconds and explicit c. Thermal geometry maintains isotropic monatomic ideal-fluid closure; active shear stress is retained.

One Lie step uses a regular fixed threshold/channel branch; O(h^2) local time error requires locally Lipschitz H_i and rate time dependence. Crossings require resolved crossing/flux treatment. Each subsequent collision rebinds actual parent/daughter energies or a conservative remap. Collision and geometry compose on this common packet state, with C_0 equal to the identity in the current chart; next-stage directions are the actually transported directions.

acceptance: Explicit finite common-event construction and positivity/invariant proof
